title: NEET UG Class 11 Revised Syllabus (NTA Updated)

Physics.name: Units and Measurements
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Units of measurements, System of Units, SI Units, fundamental and derived units
Least count, significant figures and rounding off rules
Errors in measurements, combination of errors and percentage errors
Dimensions of physical quantities, dimensional formulae and dimensional equations
Dimensional analysis and its applications: checking equation consistency, unit conversion, deducing relations
Physics.keyConcepts: Dimensional homogeneity, Least count of Vernier calipers & Screw gauge, fractional and percentage error propagation

Physics.name: Motion in a Straight Line
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Frame of reference, Motion in a straight line, Position-time graph
Speed and velocity, Uniform and non-uniform motion
Average speed and instantaneous velocity
Uniformly accelerated motion, velocity-time and position-time graphs
Kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion (calculus & graphical derivation)
Free fall under gravity and relative velocity in 1D
Physics.keyConcepts: v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at², v² - u² = 2as, Stopping distance, Area under v-t graph = displacement

Physics.name: Motion in a Plane
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Scalars and vectors, vector addition and subtraction, zero vector
Resolution of a vector in a plane, rectangular components, scalar and vector products
Motion in a plane with constant acceleration
Projectile motion: trajectory equation, maximum height, time of flight, horizontal range
Uniform circular motion, centripetal acceleration, angular velocity and frequency
Physics.keyConcepts: R = (u² sin 2θ)/g, H = (u² sin² θ)/2g, T = (2u sin θ)/g, a_c = v²/r = ω²r, Dot & cross products

Physics.name: Laws of Motion
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Intuitive concept of force, Inertia, Newton's first law of motion
Momentum and Newton's second law of motion; Impulse
Newton's third law of motion, action-reaction pairs
Law of conservation of linear momentum and its applications (rocket propulsion, gun recoil)
Equilibrium of concurrent forces, Free Body Diagrams (FBD)
Friction: static and kinetic friction, laws of friction, rolling friction, coefficient of friction
Dynamics of uniform circular motion: centripetal force, vehicle on banked and unbanked curved roads
Physics.keyConcepts: F = dp/dt = ma, Impulse = F·Δt = Δp, f_s ≤ μ_s N, v_max = √(μrg), v_opt = √(rg tan θ)

Physics.name: Work, Energy & Power
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Work done by a constant force and a variable force (W = ∫ F dx)
Kinetic energy, Work-Energy Theorem for constant and variable forces
Potential energy, potential energy function of a spring (U = 0.5 k x²)
Conservative and non-conservative forces, conservation of mechanical energy
Motion in a vertical circle (critical velocities at bottom, top and horizontal points)
Power: instantaneous and average power (P = F·v)
Collisions: elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions, coefficient of restitution
Physics.keyConcepts: W_net = ΔK, v_bottom ≥ √(5gR), v_top ≥ √(gR), e = (v2 - v1)/(u1 - u2), P = dW/dt = F·v

Physics.unitName: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
Physics.name: Rotational Motion
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Centre of mass of a two-particle system and rigid bodies
Basic concepts of rotational motion: angular displacement, velocity, acceleration
Moment of a force, torque (τ = r × F), angular momentum (L = r × p)
Conservation of angular momentum and its applications
Moment of inertia (I = ∑ m_i r_i²), radius of gyration (k = √(I/M))
Values of moment of inertia for ring, disc, cylinder, sphere, rod
Parallel and perpendicular axes theorems (qualitative and applications)
Kinematics and dynamics of rotational motion, rolling without slipping (K = K_trans + K_rot)
Physics.keyConcepts: τ = Iα, L = Iω, K_total = 0.5 M v² (1 + k²/R²), Acceleration on incline = (g sin θ)/(1 + k²/R²)

Physics.name: Gravitation
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Universal law of gravitation, gravitational constant G
Acceleration due to gravity g and its variation with altitude, depth, and latitude (earth's rotation)
Kepler's laws of planetary motion (law of orbits, areas, periods)
Gravitational potential energy (U = -GMm/r) and gravitational potential (V = -GM/r)
Escape velocity from surface of Earth (v_e = √(2gR))
Motion of a satellite, orbital velocity (v_o = √(gR)), time period and total energy of satellite
Geostationary and polar satellites, weightlessness
Physics.keyConcepts: g_h = g(1 - 2h/R), g_d = g(1 - d/R), v_e = √(2) v_o = 11.2 km/s, T² ∝ R³, Total Energy = -GMm/2r

Physics.name: Mechanical Properties of Solids
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Elastic behaviour of materials, Stress-strain relationship and curve
Hooke's law, Young's modulus, Bulk modulus, Shear modulus of rigidity
Poisson's ratio, elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire
Physics.keyConcepts: Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L), Energy density = 0.5 × Stress × Strain, Breaking stress = constant for material

Physics.name: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Pressure due to a fluid column, Pascal's law and its applications (hydraulic lift)
Viscosity, coefficient of viscosity, Stokes' law, terminal velocity
Streamline and turbulent flow, critical velocity, Reynolds number
Bernoulli's principle and its applications (Venturimeter, dynamic lift)
Surface tension and surface energy, angle of contact
Excess pressure inside liquid drop (2T/R) and soap bubble (4T/R)
Capillary rise (h = 2T cos θ / rρg)
Physics.keyConcepts: P + 0.5ρv² + ρgh = constant, v_t = 2r²(ρ - σ)g / 9η, Capillary height formula, Continuity equation A1v1 = A2v2

Physics.name: Thermal Properties of Matter
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Heat, temperature, thermal expansion (linear, superficial, volume expansion)
Specific heat capacity, molar heat capacity, calorimetry and water equivalent
Change of state, latent heat of fusion and vaporization
Heat transfer: conduction (thermal conductivity k), convection, radiation
Blackbody radiation, Wien's displacement law, Stefan-Boltzmann law
Newton's law of cooling and its experimental verification
Physics.keyConcepts: ΔL = LαΔT, Q = mcΔT, Q = mL, H = kA(T1 - T2)/L, λ_m T = b, E = σeAT⁴, dQ/dt = -k(T - T0)

Physics.name: Thermodynamics
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Thermal equilibrium, Zeroth law of thermodynamics, concept of temperature
Heat, work and internal energy, First law of thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
Thermodynamic state variables, equation of state, P-V diagrams
Isothermal process (W = nRT ln(V2/V1)), Adiabatic process (PV^γ = const, W = (P1V1 - P2V2)/(γ - 1))
Isochoric and Isobaric processes, cyclic processes (Work = area of P-V loop)
Second law of thermodynamics: reversible and irreversible processes
Heat engines and refrigerators (Carnot engine efficiency η = 1 - T2/T1)
Physics.keyConcepts: ΔU = n C_v ΔT, C_p - C_v = R, γ = C_p/C_v, Carnot efficiency η = 1 - T_c/T_h, COP = T2/(T1 - T2)

Physics.name: Kinetic Theory of Gases
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Equation of state of a perfect gas, work done in compressing a gas
Kinetic theory of gases: postulates, concept of pressure (P = (1/3) ρ v_rms²)
Kinetic interpretation of temperature, RMS, average, and most probable speeds
Degrees of freedom (f), law of equipartition of energy
Specific heat capacities of monoatomic, diatomic, and polyatomic gases
Mean free path (λ = 1 / (√2 n π d²)), Avogadro's number
Physics.keyConcepts: v_rms = √(3RT/M), v_avg = √(8RT/πM), v_mp = √(2RT/M), C_v = (f/2)R, C_p = (1 + f/2)R

Physics.name: Oscillations (SHM)
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Periodic and oscillatory motion, period, frequency, displacement relation
Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM) and its differential equation (d²x/dt² + ω²x = 0)
Phase and phase difference, velocity and acceleration in SHM
Energy in SHM: kinetic and potential energies, total energy conservation
Oscillations of a loaded spring: spring constant, combinations in series and parallel
Simple pendulum: derivation of expression for time period (T = 2π √(L/g))
Physics.keyConcepts: x = A sin(ωt + φ), v = ω√(A² - x²), a = -ω²x, E_total = 0.5 m ω² A², T_spring = 2π √(m/k)

Physics.name: Waves
Physics.subject: Physics
topics: Wave motion: transverse and longitudinal waves, speed of wave motion
Newton's formula and Laplace's correction for speed of sound in gases
Displacement relation for a progressive harmonic wave: y = A sin(kx - ωt + φ)
Principle of superposition of waves, reflection of waves
Standing/Stationary waves in strings and organ pipes (open and closed pipes)
Fundamental mode, harmonics and overtones
Beats: phenomenon, beat frequency (f_beat = |f1 - f2|)
Physics.keyConcepts: v = √(γP/ρ), Closed organ pipe: f = (2n-1)v/4L, Open organ pipe: f = nv/2L, Beat frequency = |f1 - f2|

Chemistry.name: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Matter and its nature, Dalton's atomic theory, Concept of atom and molecule
Laws of chemical combination, Atomic and molecular masses
Mole concept and molar mass, Avogadro's number
Percentage composition, empirical and molecular formulae
Chemical reactions, stoichiometry and stoichiometric calculations
Limiting reagent concept, concentration terms: Molarity, Molality, Mole fraction, ppm
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Mole = Weight / Molar Mass = N / N_A, Limiting Reagent calculation, M = n/V(L), m = n/kg solvent

Chemistry.name: Structure of Atom
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Electromagnetic radiation, Planck's quantum theory, Photoelectric effect
Atomic spectrum of hydrogen, Rydberg formula (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series)
Bohr's model: postulates, radius (r_n = 0.529 n²/Z Å), energy (E_n = -13.6 Z²/n² eV)
Dual nature of matter: de Broglie relation (λ = h/mv = h/√(2mE))
Heisenberg uncertainty principle (Δx · Δp ≥ h/4π)
Quantum mechanical model: quantum numbers (n, l, m, s) and their physical significance
Shapes of s, p, and d orbitals, nodes and nodal planes
Rules for filling electrons: Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity
Chemistry.keyConcepts: 1/λ = R_H Z² (1/n1² - 1/n2²), Total nodes = n - 1, Radial nodes = n - l - 1, Angular nodes = l

Chemistry.name: Classification of Elements & Periodicity
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Modern periodic law and present form of periodic table (s, p, d, f blocks)
IUPAC nomenclature for elements with atomic number > 100
Periodic trends in physical properties: atomic and ionic radii, lanthanoid contraction
Ionization enthalpy (IE1, IE2 trends, exceptions like Be vs B, N vs O)
Electron gain enthalpy (trends, exceptions like Cl > F, S > O)
Electronegativity (Pauling scale), valence and oxidation states, diagonal relationship
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Ionic radii of isoelectronic species ∝ 1/Z, Cl has highest negative electron gain enthalpy, Inert pair effect

Chemistry.name: Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Kossel-Lewis approach to chemical bonding, octet rule and its limitations
Ionic bond: lattice enthalpy, Born-Haber cycle, Fajan's rules (polarization, covalent character)
Covalent bond: Lewis dot structures, formal charge, resonance
Dipole moment and percentage ionic character (μ = q × d)
VSEPR theory: predicting shapes and geometries of molecules (lone pair-bond pair repulsions)
Valence Bond Theory (VBT): orbital overlap (σ and π bonds), hybridization (sp, sp², sp³, sp³d, sp³d²)
Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT): bonding and antibonding MOs, bond order, magnetic properties (O2 paramagnetic, B2, C2, N2)
Hydrogen bonding: intermolecular and intramolecular H-bonds and their effects on physical properties
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Bond Order = 0.5 (N_b - N_a), Hybridization steric number formula, Fajan's rules: small cation + large anion = covalent

Chemistry.name: Chemical Thermodynamics
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: System and surroundings, types of systems, extensive and intensive properties, state functions
First law of thermodynamics: internal energy (U), heat (q), work (w = -P_ext ΔV), ΔU = q + w
Enthalpy (H = U + PV), relation between ΔH and ΔU (ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT)
Heat capacity (C), specific heat, molar heat capacity (C_p - C_v = R)
Hess's law of constant heat summation and its applications
Standard enthalpy of reaction, formation, combustion, bond dissociation, atomization, solution
Second law of thermodynamics: Spontaneity, Entropy (S), ΔS_system and ΔS_surroundings
Gibbs free energy (G = H - TS), Gibbs-Helmholtz equation (ΔG = ΔH - TΔS)
Standard free energy change and equilibrium constant (ΔG° = -RT ln K)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: ΔG < 0 for spontaneity, ΔG° = -2.303 RT log K_eq, Hess's Law cycles, Bond Enthalpy: ΔH_rxn = ∑BE_reactants - ∑BE_products

Chemistry.name: Equilibrium (Physical & Chemical)
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Dynamic nature of equilibrium in physical and chemical processes
Law of mass action, equilibrium constants K_p and K_c and their relation (K_p = K_c (RT)^Δn_g)
Reaction quotient Q and predicting the direction of reaction
Factors affecting equilibrium: Le Chatelier's principle (concentration, pressure, temperature, catalyst, inert gas)
Ionic equilibrium: Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry, and Lewis concepts of acids and bases
Ionization of water, pH scale, ionization constants of weak acids (K_a) and weak bases (K_b), Ostwald's dilution law
Common ion effect, Hydrolysis of salts and pH of salt solutions
Buffer solutions: acidic buffer, basic buffer, Henderson-Hasselbalch equation
Solubility product constant (K_sp), common ion effect on solubility, condition for precipitation (Q_sp > K_sp)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: pH = -log[H+], Henderson eq: pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid]), K_p = K_c(RT)^Δn, K_sp = s^(x+y) · x^x · y^y

Chemistry.name: Redox Reactions
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Classical and electronic concepts of oxidation and reduction
Oxidation number: rules for assignment, exceptional oxidation states (CrO5, H2SO5, Fe3O4)
Types of redox reactions: combination, decomposition, displacement, disproportionation
Balancing of redox reactions by oxidation number method and ion-electron (half-reaction) method
Applications of redox reactions, redox titrations
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Disproportionation reactions, Balancing in acidic (H+, H2O) and basic (OH-, H2O) mediums, Oxidation number tricks

Chemistry.name: p-Block Elements (Group 13 & 14)
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Group 13 Elements (Boron family): Electronic configuration, oxidation states (+3, +1), inert pair effect
Anomalous properties of Boron, Boron hydrides (Diborane structure - 3c-2e banana bonds), Boric acid, Borax
Group 14 Elements (Carbon family): Electronic configuration, oxidation states (+4, +2), catenation ability
Allotropes of carbon: diamond, graphite, fullerenes (buckminsterfullerene C60), carbon nanotubes
Oxides of carbon (CO, CO2), Silicones, Silicates, and Zeolites
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Inert pair effect: Tl+ > Tl3+, Pb2+ > Pb4+, Diborane banana bonds (two 3-centre-2-electron bonds), Catenation C >> Si > Ge ≈ Sn

Chemistry.unitName: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles & Techniques
Chemistry.name: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles (GOC)
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: General introduction, tetravalence of carbon, hybridization (sp³, sp², sp), shapes of simple molecules
Classification of organic compounds and functional groups
IUPAC nomenclature of aliphatic, alicyclic, and aromatic compounds
Isomerism: Structural isomerism (chain, position, functional, metamerism, tautomerism)
Stereoisomerism: Geometrical isomerism (cis-trans, E-Z), Optical isomerism (chirality, enantiomers, diastereomers, meso)
Electronic displacements in a covalent bond: Inductive effect (+I, -I), Electromeric effect (+E, -E)
Resonance and Mesomeric effect (+M, -M), Hyperconjugation (Baker-Nathan effect), Aromaticity (Hückel's 4n+2 rule)
Homolytic and heterolytic fission, Reactive intermediates: Carbocations, Carbanions, Free radicals (stability orders)
Electrophiles and Nucleophiles, types of organic reactions (substitution, addition, elimination, rearrangement)
Purification methods and qualitative/quantitative analysis (Dumas, Kjeldahl methods)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Stability: 3° > 2° > 1° for carbocations & radicals; 1° > 2° > 3° for carbanions; -I/-M increases acidic strength; Kjeldahl N% formula

Chemistry.name: Hydrocarbons
Chemistry.subject: Chemistry
topics: Classification of hydrocarbons: Alkanes, Alkenes, Alkynes, Arenes
Alkanes: Nomenclature, conformations of ethane (sawhorse and Newman projections), physical properties
Chemical reactions of alkanes: Free radical halogenation mechanism, combustion, pyrolysis, aromatization
Alkenes: Structure of double bond, geometrical isomerism, methods of preparation (dehydrohalogenation, Kolbe's synthesis)
Reactions of alkenes: Electrophilic addition of H2, X2, H2O, HX (Markovnikov's rule and Kharasch peroxide effect)
Ozonolysis and reductive cleavage with Zn/H2O, oxidation with Baeyer's reagent (cold alkaline KMnO4)
Alkynes: Structure of triple bond, acidic character of terminal alkynes (HC≡CH + NaNH2)
Addition reactions of alkynes: hydrogenation (Lindlar catalyst vs Na/liq NH3), halogenation, hydration (Kucherov reaction)
Aromatic hydrocarbons (Arenes): Benzene structure, resonance, aromaticity
Electrophilic aromatic substitution: Mechanism of nitration, sulphonation, halogenation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation & acylation
Directive influence of substituents in mono-substituted benzene (o,p-directing vs m-directing groups)
Chemistry.keyConcepts: Markovnikov vs Anti-Markovnikov addition, Ozonolysis predicts original alkene structure, Terminal alkynes acidic, Friedel-Crafts carbocation rearrangements

Biology.name: The Living World
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: What is living? Defining features vs non-defining characteristics of life (Growth, Reproduction, Metabolism, Cellular organization, Consciousness)
Biodiversity and need for classification
Taxonomy and Systematics, identification, nomenclature
Binomial nomenclature: rules formulated by ICBN and ICZN
Taxonomic categories: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum/Division, Kingdom (taxonomical hierarchy)
Species concept and biological species definition
Biology.keyConcepts: Metabolism & consciousness are defining properties, Binomial rules: genus capitalized, species lowercase, Latin/italics

Biology.name: Biological Classification
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Five kingdom classification proposed by R.H. Whittaker (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia)
Kingdom Monera: Archaebacteria (methanogens, halophiles, thermoacidophiles), Eubacteria, cyanobacteria, mycoplasma
Kingdom Protista: Chrysophytes (diatoms, desmids), Dinoflagellates, Euglenoids, Slime moulds, Protozoans
Kingdom Fungi: Morphology, reproduction, classification into Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes
Viruses, Viroids, Prions, and Lichens: Discovery, structural components, infectious nature, disease examples
Biology.keyConcepts: Diatomaceous earth cell walls (silica), Mycoplasma lack cell wall & are resistant to penicillin, Fungi classes: spore types & fruiting bodies

Biology.name: Plant Kingdom
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Systems of classification: Artificial, Natural (Bentham & Hooker), and Phylogenetic
Algae: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyceae (pigments, stored food, cell wall composition, flagella)
Bryophytes: Amphibians of plant kingdom, Liverworts and Mosses, gametophyte dominant generation, economic importance of Sphagnum
Pteridophytes: First vascular land plants, sporophyte dominant, homospory vs heterospory, seed habit precursor (Selaginella, Salvinia)
Gymnosperms: Naked seeded plants, Coralloid roots (Cycas) with cyanobacteria, mycorrhiza (Pinus), reproduction and cones
Biology.keyConcepts: Algal pigments (fucoxanthin, r-phycoerythrin), Stored food (floridean starch, laminarin), Heterospory leads to seed habit, Gymnosperms lack vessels & companion cells

Biology.name: Animal Kingdom
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Basis of classification: Levels of organization, symmetry, diploblastic vs triploblastic, coelom, segmentation, notochord
Non-chordate phyla: Porifera, Coelenterata (Cnidaria), Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Hemichordata
Diagnostic characters and NCERT examples of each non-chordate phylum
Phylum Chordata: Fundamental characters (notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits)
Subphyla: Urochordata, Cephalochordata, Vertebrata
Vertebrata classes: Cyclostomata, Chondrichthyes, Osteichthyes, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia
Biology.keyConcepts: Coelom types (Acoelomate, Pseudocoelomate, Eucoelomate), Arthropoda open circulatory system & chitinous exoskeleton, Water vascular system in Echinodermata

Biology.unitName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
Biology.name: Morphology of Flowering Plants
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Root modifications for storage, support (prop & stilt roots), respiration (pneumatophores)
Stem modifications: tendrils, thorns, phylloclade, runners, stolons, offsets, rhizome, tuber
Leaf: parts, venation (reticulate & parallel), types of leaves (simple & compound), phyllotaxy, modifications
Inflorescence: Racemose and Cymose
Flower: parts (calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium), symmetry (actinomorphic, zygomorphic), ovary position (hypogynous, perigynous, epigynous)
Aestivation (valvate, twisted, imbricate, vexillary), Placentation (marginal, axile, parietal, free central, basal)
Fruit (drupe, berry, true vs false fruits), Seed (monocot & dicot structure)
Detailed description of angiosperm families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Fabaceae/Leguminosae, Solanaceae, Compositae, Gramineae
Biology.keyConcepts: Floral formula and diagrams, Placentation examples, Vexillary aestivation in Pea, Axile placentation in Tomato & Citrus, Pneumatophores in Rhizophora

Biology.unitName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
Biology.name: Anatomy of Flowering Plants
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Meristematic tissues: apical, intercalary, and lateral meristems
Simple permanent tissues: Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma (fibres and sclereids)
Complex permanent tissues: Xylem (tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma) and Phloem (sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres, phloem parenchyma)
Tissue systems: Epidermal, Ground, and Vascular tissue systems (radial, conjoint, collateral, open vs closed)
Anatomy of Dicot and Monocot Root (endodermis, Casparian strips, radial bundles)
Anatomy of Dicot and Monocot Stem (hypodermis, ring vs scattered vascular bundles)
Anatomy of Dorsiventral (Dicot) and Isobilateral (Monocot) Leaf (mesophyll, stomata, bulliform cells)
Biology.keyConcepts: Casparian strips made of suberin in endodermis, Collenchyma provides mechanical support with pectin corners, Bulliform cells in grasses curl leaves

Biology.unitName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
Biology.name: Structural Organisation in Animals
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Animal tissues: Epithelial tissue (Simple: squamous, cuboidal, columnar, ciliated; Compound epithelial)
Connective tissue: Loose (areolar, adipose), Dense (regular, irregular), Specialized (cartilage, bone, blood)
Muscular tissue: Skeletal (striated/voluntary), Smooth (unstriated/involuntary), Cardiac muscle
Neural tissue: Neurons and Neuroglial cells
Morphology, anatomy, and digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous, and reproductive systems of Frog (Rana tigrina)
Morphology and basic systems of Cockroach (Periplaneta americana)
Biology.keyConcepts: Tight, adhering, and gap junctions in epithelia, Haversian canals in mammalian bones, Frog cutaneous & pulmonary respiration, 3-chambered heart

Biology.name: Cell: The Unit of Life
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Cell theory: Schleiden, Schwann, and Rudolf Virchow (Omnis cellula-e cellula)
Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic cells: size, genetic material, mesosomes, inclusion bodies
Cell envelope: Glycocalyx, cell wall, and plasma membrane (Fluid Mosaic Model by Singer and Nicolson)
Endomembrane system: Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER, SER), Golgi apparatus, Lysosomes, Vacuoles
Mitochondria: semi-autonomous nature, double membrane, cristae, 70S ribosomes, circular DNA
Plastids: Chloroplasts, Chromoplasts, Leucoplasts (Amyloplast, Elaioplast, Aleuroplast)
Ribosomes: 70S (prokaryotic & organelles) and 80S (eukaryotic cytoplasm), Polysomes
Cytoskeleton: Microtubules, microfilaments, intermediate filaments
Cilia and Flagella (9+2 axoneme arrangement), Centrosome and Centrioles (9+0 arrangement)
Nucleus: Nuclear envelope, chromatin, nucleolus, chromosomes (metacentric, sub-metacentric, acrocentric, telocentric)
Biology.keyConcepts: Fluid Mosaic Model lipid bilayer with intrinsic proteins, Mitochondria & Chloroplast endosymbiotic origin, Peroxisomes, Centrioles lack DNA

Biology.name: Biomolecules
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Chemical analysis of living tissues (acid-soluble pool vs acid-insoluble retentate)
Carbohydrates: Monosaccharides (reducing vs non-reducing sugars), Disaccharides, Polysaccharides (starch, glycogen, cellulose, chitin)
Lipids: Fatty acids (saturated vs unsaturated), glycerol, triglycerides, phospholipids (lecithin)
Proteins: Amino acids (zwitterion, essential vs non-essential), peptide bonds, primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures
Nucleic acids: Nucleotides (nitrogenous bases, pentose sugar, phosphate), phosphodiester bonds, Watson-Crick DNA B-form model
Nature of bonds linking monomers: peptide, glycosidic, phosphodiester bonds
Metabolic basis of living: anabolic vs catabolic pathways, living state as non-equilibrium steady state
Enzymes: Chemical nature, activation energy diagram, mechanism of enzyme action (lock and key, induced fit)
Factors affecting enzyme activity: Temperature, pH, substrate concentration (K_m value)
Enzyme inhibition: Competitive (e.g. malonate inhibiting succinate dehydrogenase), non-competitive
Classification and nomenclature of enzymes (Oxidoreductases, Transferases, Hydrolases, Lyases, Isomerases, Ligases), Co-factors
Biology.keyConcepts: Competitive inhibitor increases K_m without changing V_max, Cellulose has beta-1,4 glycosidic bonds, Collagen is most abundant protein in animals, RuBisCO in biosphere

Biology.name: Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Cell cycle: Phases of cell cycle - Interphase (G1, S, G2 phases) and M Phase (Mitosis)
G0 phase (quiescent stage) and cell cycle checkpoints
Mitosis: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase; Cytokinesis (cell plate vs furrow method)
Significance of mitosis in growth, repair, and regeneration
Meiosis: Meiosis I (Prophase I: Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene, Diakinesis), Metaphase I, Anaphase I, Telophase I
Synaptonemal complex, bivalents, tetrads, crossing over (recombinase enzyme), chiasmata formation
Interkinesis, Meiosis II (equation division)
Significance of meiosis: genetic variation and maintenance of chromosome number across generations
Biology.keyConcepts: Crossing over occurs in Pachytene with recombinase, Chiasmata seen in Diplotene, DNA doubles in S phase but chromosome number remains same

Biology.name: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Early experiments: Priestley, Ingenhousz, Senebier, Engelmann, Cornelius van Niel
Site of photosynthesis, chloroplast structure, photosynthetic pigments (chlorophyll a, b, carotenoids, xanthophylls)
Absorption spectrum vs action spectrum
Light reaction (Photochemical phase): Light harvesting complexes (LHC), PS I and PS II, reaction centres (P700 and P680)
Electron transport, Z-scheme, photolysis of water (oxygen evolving complex, Mn and Cl ions)
Cyclic and Non-cyclic photophosphorylation, Chemiosmotic hypothesis (Peter Mitchell) and ATP synthesis (CF0-CF1 particles)
Dark reaction (Biosynthetic phase): Calvin cycle (C3 pathway) - Carboxylation (RuBisCO), Reduction, Regeneration
C4 pathway (Hatch-Slack pathway): Kranz anatomy, bundle sheath cells, PEP carboxylase, adaptation to high light and temp
Photorespiration (C2 cycle): role of RuBisCO as oxygenase, waste of ATP and carbon in C3 plants
Factors affecting photosynthesis: Blackman's law of limiting factors, light, CO2 concentration, temperature, water
Biology.keyConcepts: Water splitting at PS II releases O2 into lumen, Calvin cycle consumes 3 ATP & 2 NADPH per CO2 fixed, C4 plants lack photorespiration, RuBisCO is oxygenase at high O2/CO2

Biology.name: Respiration in Plants
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Cellular respiration: aerobic vs anaerobic respiration, respiratory substrates
Glycolysis (EMP pathway): 10 enzymatic steps, site (cytoplasm), key enzymes (hexokinase, PFK), ATP accounting
Fermentation: Alcoholic fermentation (pyruvate decarboxylase & alcohol dehydrogenase) and Lactic acid fermentation
Link reaction: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to Acetyl CoA by Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
Krebs cycle (TCA cycle / Citric acid cycle): Mitochondrial matrix, cyclical reactions, GTP synthesis, FADH2 and NADH production
Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation: Complexes I, II, III, IV, V, mobile carriers (Ubiquinone, Cytochrome c)
Terminal electron acceptor (O2), Proton gradient across inner mitochondrial membrane
Respiratory balance sheet (net 36 or 38 ATP generated per glucose), Amphibolic nature of respiration
Respiratory Quotient (RQ = CO2 evolved / O2 consumed): RQ of carbohydrates (1.0), fats (0.7), proteins (0.9), organic acids (>1)
Biology.keyConcepts: Glycolysis net 2 ATP + 2 NADH, Cytochrome c oxidase complex IV contains copper centers, RQ of tripalmitin = 0.7, Complex V is ATP synthase

Biology.name: Plant Growth and Development
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Characteristics of plant growth: indeterminate, open form, phases of growth (meristematic, elongation, maturation)
Growth rates: Arithmetic growth (L_t = L_0 + rt) and Geometric growth (W_1 = W_0 e^rt, sigmoid curve)
Conditions for growth: water, oxygen, nutrients, light, temperature
Differentiation, Dedifferentiation, and Redifferentiation with examples
Plasticity: Heterophylly in cotton, coriander, larkspur, and buttercup
Plant Growth Regulators (Phytohormones): Discovery, physiological roles, and agricultural applications of:
- Auxins (IAA, NAA, 2,4-D): apical dominance, rooting, weedicide
- Gibberellins (GA3): bolting, elongation of sugarcane stems, malt production
- Cytokinins (Zeatin, Kinetin): cell division, delaying senescence, overcoming apical dominance
- Ethylene (gaseous hormone): fruit ripening, triple response, femaleness in cucumber
- Abscisic Acid (ABA): stress hormone, stomatal closure, seed dormancy
Biology.keyConcepts: Apical dominance caused by auxin, overcome by cytokinin; GA causes bolting in rosette plants; 2,4-D kills broad-leaved dicot weeds; ABA is antitranspirant

Biology.name: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Respiratory organs in different animals
Human respiratory system: Nostrils, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli, lungs, pleura
Mechanism of breathing: Inspiration (diaphragm and external intercostals) and Expiration, pressure gradients
Respiratory volumes and capacities: Tidal Volume (TV), IRV, ERV, Residual Volume (RV), Inspiratory Capacity (IC), FRC, Vital Capacity (VC), Total Lung Capacity (TLC)
Exchange of gases at alveoli and tissue levels: Partial pressures (pO2, pCO2)
Transport of gases in blood: Oxygen transport (Oxyhaemoglobin, Oxygen dissociation curve, Bohr effect)
Carbon dioxide transport (dissolved plasma, carbamino-haemoglobin, bicarbonate ions via carbonic anhydrase, Haldane effect)
Regulation of respiration: Respiratory rhythm centre (medulla), pneumotaxic centre (pons), chemosensitive area
Respiratory disorders: Asthma, Emphysema (loss of alveolar surface area), Occupational respiratory disorders (Silicosis, Asbestosis)
Biology.keyConcepts: Oxygen dissociation curve is sigmoid; Right shift: high pCO2, high H+ (low pH), high temperature; TV = 500 mL, VC = TV + IRV + ERV

Biology.name: Body Fluids and Circulation
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Composition of blood: Plasma (water, albumin, globulin, fibrinogen) and Formed elements (RBCs, WBCs: granulocytes & agranulocytes, Platelets)
Blood groups: ABO system, Rh grouping, Erythroblastosis foetalis (Rh incompatibility)
Coagulation of blood: Clotting cascade, thromboplastin, prothrombinase, thrombin, fibrin, role of Ca2+ ions
Lymph (tissue fluid): composition and functions
Circulatory pathways: open vs closed circulatory systems, evolution of vertebrate hearts
Human circulatory system: Heart anatomy, nodal tissues (SA node / pacemaker, AV node, Bundle of His, Purkinje fibres)
Cardiac cycle: Joint diastole, atrial systole, ventricular systole, Heart sounds (Lubb, Dubb), Cardiac output (Stroke volume × Heart rate)
Electrocardiogram (ECG): P wave (atrial depolarization), QRS complex (ventricular depolarization), T wave (ventricular repolarization)
Double circulation: Pulmonary and Systemic circulation, Hepatic portal system
Regulation of cardiac activity: Autonomic nervous system (Sympathetic increases HR, Parasympathetic decreases HR), Adrenal medullary hormones
Disorders of circulatory system: Hypertension, Atherosclerosis / Coronary Artery Disease (CAD), Angina pectoris, Heart failure
Biology.keyConcepts: SA node 70-75 bpm intrinsic rhythm, Lubb sound by AV valve closure, Dubb by semilunar closure, Stroke volume = 70 mL, Cardiac output = 5 L/min

Biology.name: Excretory Products and Their Elimination
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Modes of excretion: Ammonotelism (bony fishes, aquatic amphibians), Ureotelism (mammals, terrestrial amphibians), Uricotelism (reptiles, birds, insects)
Human excretory system: Kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, urethra
Structure of nephron: Cortical and Juxtamedullary nephrons, Glomerulus, Bowman's capsule, PCT, Loop of Henle, DCT, Collecting duct
Mechanism of urine formation: Glomerular filtration (GFR = 125 mL/min = 180 L/day), Tubular reabsorption, Tubular secretion
Function of the tubules: PCT (70-80% electrolytes & water reabsorbed), Henle's loop, DCT, Collecting duct
Mechanism of concentration of the filtrate: Counter-current mechanism in Loop of Henle and Vasa Recta (NaCl and Urea recycling)
Regulation of kidney function: Hypothalamus and ADH (Vasopressin), Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF)
Micturition reflex and composition of urine
Role of other organs in excretion: Lungs (CO2), Liver (bilirubin, biliverdin), Skin (sweat, sebum)
Disorders of excretory system: Uraemia, Renal calculi (stones of calcium oxalate), Glomerulonephritis, Haemodialysis, Kidney transplantation
Biology.keyConcepts: Counter current creates 300 to 1200 mOsm/L gradient, ADH increases water reabsorption via aquaporins, RAAS increases BP & GFR, ANF causes vasodilation

Biology.name: Locomotion and Movement
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Types of movement in humans: Amoeboid (macrophages), Ciliary (trachea, fallopian tubes), Flagellar (spermatozoa), Muscular
Skeletal muscle: Fascia, muscle fascicles, muscle fibres, Sarcolemma, Sarcoplasmic reticulum (storehouse of Ca2+)
Ultrastructure of myofibril: Sarcomere (functional unit of contraction), A-band, I-band, H-zone, Z-line, M-line
Contractile proteins: Actin (F-actin, Tropomyosin, Troponin complex) and Myosin (Meromyosin: HMM with cross arm & LMM)
Sliding Filament Theory of muscle contraction: Neuromuscular junction, acetylcholine, Action potential, Ca2+ binding to troponin C, cross-bridge cycle, ATP hydrolysis
Red muscle fibres (aerobic, myoglobin rich, many mitochondria) vs White muscle fibres (anaerobic, fast twitch, rich in SR)
Human skeletal system: Axial skeleton (80 bones: skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum) and Appendicular skeleton (126 bones: limbs and girdles)
Joints: Fibrous (synarthroses / sutures), Cartilaginous (amphiarthroses / pubic symphysis), Synovial (diarthroses: ball and socket, hinge, pivot, gliding, saddle)
Disorders of muscular and skeletal system: Myasthenia gravis (autoimmune), Tetany (low Ca2+), Muscular dystrophy, Arthritis, Osteoporosis (decreased estrogen), Gout (uric acid crystals)
Biology.keyConcepts: During contraction: I-band shortens, H-zone disappears, A-band length remains constant; Tropomyosin covers myosin binding site on actin; Troponin C binds Ca2+

Biology.name: Neural Control and Coordination
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Coordination and neural system in animals (Hydra network, insects ladder, vertebrates brain)
Human neural system: Central Nervous System (CNS) and Peripheral Nervous System (PNS: Somatic & Autonomic)
Structure of a typical neuron: Cyton, Dendrites, Axon, Myelin sheath (Schwann cells), Nodes of Ranvier, Synaptic knobs
Generation and conduction of nerve impulse: Resting membrane potential (-70 mV, Na+/K+ ATPase pump: 3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in)
Action potential (+30 mV) / depolarization by rapid Na+ influx via voltage-gated channels, repolarization by K+ efflux
Transmission of impulses across synapses: Electrical synapse (gap junctions, faster) and Chemical synapse (neurotransmitters like Acetylcholine)
Central nervous system: Meninges (Duramater, Arachnoid, Piamater)
Forebrain: Cerebrum (cerebral cortex, corpus callosum, sensory/motor/association areas), Thalamus, Hypothalamus, Limbic system
Midbrain: Corpora quadrigemina, cerebral aqueduct
Hindbrain: Pons, Cerebellum (arbor vitae, balance), Medulla oblongata (cardiac, respiratory, gastric centres)
Biology.keyConcepts: Na+/K+ pump pumps 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in consuming 1 ATP, Corpus callosum connects left & right cerebral hemispheres, Hypothalamus controls thermoregulation & hunger

Biology.name: Chemical Coordination and Integration
Biology.subject: Biology
topics: Endocrine glands and hormones (non-nutrient chemicals acting as intercellular messengers)
Hypothalamus: Releasing and inhibiting hormones, neurohypophysial regulation
Pituitary gland: Adenohypophysis (GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, MSH) and Neurohypophysis (Oxytocin, Vasopressin/ADH)
Pineal gland: Melatonin and 24-hour diurnal circadian rhythm, sleep-wake cycle
Thyroid gland: Follicular cells (T3, T4 / thyroxine, Iodine requirement) and Parafollicular cells (Thyrocalcitonin - TCT decreases blood Ca2+)
Parathyroid gland: Parathyroid hormone (PTH / hypercalcemic hormone increases blood Ca2+)
Thymus gland: Thymosins, cell-mediated immunity (T-lymphocytes) and humoral immunity
Adrenal gland: Adrenal cortex (Mineralocorticoids/Aldosterone, Glucocorticoids/Cortisol, Androgens) and Adrenal medulla (Adrenaline and Noradrenaline / catecholamines / fight-or-flight)
Pancreas (Islets of Langerhans): Alpha cells (Glucagon / hyper-glycemic) and Beta cells (Insulin / hypo-glycemic)
Gonads: Testes (Leydig cells produce Testosterone) and Ovaries (Estrogen by growing follicles, Progesterone by Corpus luteum)
Hormones of non-endocrine tissues: Heart (ANF), Kidney (Erythropoietin), Gastrointestinal tract (Gastrin, Secretin, CCK, GIP)

Mechanism of hormone action: Protein/Peptide hormones (membrane receptors, secondary messengers: cAMP, IP3, Ca2+) vs Steroid & Thyroid hormones (intracellular nuclear receptors, gene expression alteration)
Endocrine disorders: Dwarfism, Gigantism, Acromegaly, Diabetes insipidus, Simple Goitre, Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease), Cretinism, Myxedema, Addison's disease, Diabetes mellitus
Biology.keyConcepts: Antagonistic pairs: Insulin vs Glucagon, Calcitonin vs PTH; Secondary messengers (cAMP, IP3, Ca2+) for protein hormones; Steroids diffuse through lipid membrane directly
